title: Statistical Analysis & Interpretation
summary: Careful descriptive and inferential analysis of your data, with results explained in plain language so you can act on them.
overview: We take a dataset and a question, choose methods whose assumptions actually fit the data, and carry out the analysis from summary statistics through to hypothesis tests and confidence intervals. The work covers measures of central tendency and dispersion, correlation, probability models, large- and small-sample tests, ANOVA and nonparametric alternatives such as chi-square and Kolmogorov-Smirnov tests. Every result comes with an explanation of what it does and does not show.
problems: You have data but are unsure which summary measures or tests are appropriate
You need to compare groups, means or proportions and judge whether differences are meaningful
Reports contain numbers without any statement of uncertainty or assumptions
Your data are skewed, categorical or small in size and standard tests may not apply
Stakeholders need findings explained without statistical jargon
audience: Managers and analysts in business, economics and management roles
Researchers who need an independent check of their analysis
Small teams without an in-house statistician
Public-sector and non-profit teams working with survey or administrative data
client_inputs: The question or decision the analysis should inform
The dataset (or an anonymised extract) with a short description of each variable
Information on how the data were collected
Any earlier analyses or reports for context
A named contact who can answer questions about the data

process.detail: We talk through the question, the data available and how the results will be used.
We set out the proposed methods, deliverables and timeline in writing for your agreement.
We check variable types, missing values and distributions, and flag issues that affect method choice.
We run descriptive summaries, estimation and the agreed tests, checking assumptions as we go.
We present the findings in a written report and a live session where you can ask questions.
We can answer follow-up questions or re-run the analysis on updated data.

deliverables: Written report with methodology, results tables and plain-language interpretation
Charts and summary tables ready to reuse in presentations
Statement of assumptions checked and limitations of the analysis
Reproducible R or Python scripts, or a documented Excel workbook
Walkthrough session recording or notes
applications: Summarising sales, cost or performance data for business and management decisions
Comparing outcomes between groups in economic and social research
Testing associations between categorical attributes in survey responses
Checking whether observed data fit an assumed distribution

Large-sample tests for means and proportions
t, F and chi-square tests

title: Regression & Predictive Modelling
summary: Regression models that explain how outcomes depend on their drivers, built and validated with transparent methods.
overview: This service builds and evaluates regression models for continuous and binary outcomes. We start from least-squares fitting and correlation, extend to multiple and polynomial regression, use cross-validation and regularised methods (ridge and lasso) to control overfitting, and apply logistic regression and discriminant analysis where the outcome is a category. The emphasis is on models you can understand and defend, with honest reporting of goodness of fit.
problems: You want to know which factors are associated with an outcome and by how much
You need to predict a quantity or a yes/no outcome from available variables
An existing model fits past data well but performs poorly on new data
Many candidate predictors make it hard to choose a sensible model
Model results need to be explained to non-technical decision makers

Researchers modelling relationships between variables
Product and data teams needing a baseline predictive model
Economists and management students working on applied projects
client_inputs: The outcome to be explained or predicted and how it is measured

process.detail: We clarify the outcome, the intended use of the model and what 'useful' means for you.
We agree on model types, validation approach and deliverables.
We explore relationships with scatter plots and correlations and prepare the predictors.
We fit candidate models, compare them using cross-validation and check residuals and assumptions.
We explain coefficients, fit measures and limitations in a written report and live session.
We hand over code and notes so your team can refit the model on new data.

deliverables: Written report with methodology, coefficient tables and plain-language interpretation

title: Machine Learning & AI Modelling
summary: Practical machine learning, from feature selection and classical algorithms to neural networks, scoped to what your data can support.
overview: We help you decide whether machine learning is the right tool, then design, train and evaluate models. Work typically starts with data pre-processing and feature selection, moves through classical techniques such as decision trees, random forests, support-vector machines, naive Bayes, k-nearest neighbours and gradient boosting, and, where justified, extends to neural networks, convolutional and recurrent architectures. Models are assessed with appropriate measures such as accuracy, precision and recall on held-out data, and we are clear about their limitations.

title: Time-Series Analysis & Forecasting
summary: Trend, seasonality and short-term forecasts from data recorded over time, plus construction of index numbers.
overview: We analyse data collected over time to separate trend, seasonal and irregular components, fit growth curves, and produce forecasts using exponential smoothing and autoregressive or moving-average models. Model order is guided by the autocorrelation function and parameters are estimated by least squares or Yule-Walker equations. We also construct simple and weighted index numbers, including Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher forms and cost-of-living indices.

Planning depends on short-term forecasts of demand, sales or volumes

title: Survival, Reliability & Biostatistical Analysis
summary: Time-to-event analysis for patients, customers or components, handling censored data correctly.
overview: Survival and reliability analysis studies how long it takes for an event to occur, whether that is a clinical outcome, a customer leaving or a component failing. We estimate survival and hazard functions with Kaplan-Meier and Nelson-Aalen methods, deal with different kinds of censoring, fit lifetime distributions such as exponential, Weibull, gamma and lognormal, and compare groups. Regression approaches such as the Cox proportional hazards model are considered where appropriate. For engineered systems, we assess reliability of series, parallel, k-out-of-n and standby configurations, and can use Markov and queuing models.

You need to compare time-to-event between treatment or customer groups

title: Statistical Quality Control & Process Monitoring
summary: Control charts and acceptance sampling plans that help you tell normal variation from real process problems.
overview: We help production and service teams monitor quality using statistical process control. We also design single and double acceptance sampling plans and describe their operating characteristics so you understand the risks of accepting or rejecting a lot.

title: Operations Research & Decision Modelling
summary: Optimisation and decision models for allocating resources, planning logistics and choosing under uncertainty.
overview: Operations research turns a planning problem into a mathematical model and finds the best feasible solution within constraints of time, labour, materials and business rules. We formulate and solve linear programmes, transportation and assignment problems, analyse competitive situations with game theory, and build decision models using payoff matrices, decision trees and the value of information. Where uncertainty is significant we use Monte-Carlo simulation, and for problems with vague criteria we can apply fuzzy multicriteria methods.

title: Mathematical Modelling & Numerical Computation
